meta.probingQuestion: What happens in you when someone makes real contact?

games.title: Chest to Chest Under Elbows Maintenance

meta.connection: Holding contact on the mat and noticing what contact does to you are the same skill. Both mean staying present when someone gets close, instead of pushing them away. The pin teaches your body to stay. Thinking about it teaches your mind why staying is hard.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, open guard, and a chest-to-chest pin. Holding a pin teaches your body to stay present instead of pushing someone away. Real contact does something to everyone, and now you can feel it. You get to notice that feeling instead of running from it.

slides.title: What happens in you when someone makes real contact?

body.text: This is locking hands around him while standing.

items: Whoever first locks his hands around his partner wins, arms under the elbows. The same rule applies to both players.

body.text: This is going around him to his chest.

items: The top player wins by going around the bottom player's legs and locking his hands around him.
The bottom player wins by making the top player's butt hit the mat and sitting up.

body.text: This is staying on top, under his elbows.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps something between the bottom player's elbows and his ribs.
The bottom player wins by getting both elbows to touch his body, or by making the top player fall.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Tonight you stayed chest to chest while he fought to pull his elbows in. What kept you there?

options.feedback: Real contact means you stay close, even when he fights it.

options.text: Lifting your chest off to rest.
options.feedback: Lifting off gives him room to escape.

options.text: Grabbing his head with both hands.
options.feedback: His elbows come free when you let go.
